messages:
liz: Heads-up — CS escalated C-8893: customer saying our quantized endpoint (mix FP8/INT8) is significantly slower and lower-quality than their FP16 baseline after the last calibration push. link: https://acme.support/8893 :grimacing:

maya: Thanks. Do we have perf/profile from the affected endpoint + model id? any recent kernel changes in deploy?

liz: CS pasted the p95 timelines and a short repro. Model: model-x-3b. Endpoint: quant-asia-1 (tenant=acme). They say FP16 p95 ~120ms, quantized p95 jumped to ~420ms since 2026-03-08 calibration run.

jonas: Poked into infra logs for that endpoint. Attaching quick sample from profiler: 
```
2026-03-14T09:12:03Z GPU0 kernel_select -> quant_kv_safe_v1 (fallback=false)
2026-03-14T09:12:03Z attention_call -> fused_attn_int8 (latency 2.1ms)
2026-03-14T09:12:03Z kv_cache -> miss (invalidated) -> rebuild_kv_slow_path (latency 18.7ms)
2026-03-14T09:12:03Z matmul -> generic_fp32 (latency 12.4ms)
```
Two oddities: 1) several matmuls choose generic_fp32 path, 2) frequent kv cache rebuilds.

rahul: My initial hypothesis: the recent calibration produced a quantization profile with outlier ranges that cause our selector to prefer a "safe" but slower kernel for a subset of layers. For attention, if fused path can't be used (due to quant type mismatch) we fall back to generic kernels and kv-cache helpers which are much slower. Also calibration touched per-layer clipping thresholds, which can change whether we can use per-token KV reuse (we invalidate early to be conservative).

maya: Repro steps requested from jonas looked valid — small prompt set triggered the worst case. Also noticed batching heuristics dropped to small batches (N<=2) because routing kept splitting requests to different quant variants. That amplified per-request overhead.

jonas: Quick workaround I tested on a canary: force routing to fp16-stable variant for tenant=acme. Results: p95 fell back to ~140ms within 10 minutes. Steps I ran: 
```bash
# quick override (canary)
rwctl routing override set --tenant acme --endpoint quant-asia-1 --target-variant fp16-stable --ttl 1h
```
No restart required.

rahul: For a medium-term fix we have two paths: 1) recalibrate quant profiles with tighter outlier clipping and run per-layer validation to ensure fused kernels remain eligible, or 2) tune kernel selection thresholds so we don't pick safe generic kernels unnecessarily (e.g., prefer fused path if estimated error < eps). Both need offline evals.

liz: Customer needs comms. Draft please, short and clear. Also want mitigation we can apply immediately (no config change that touches other tenants).

maya: Draft for CS (short):
"Hi — we tracked this to a calibration change that made the quantized runtime pick a slower execution path for some layers. We've temporarily routed your traffic to the FP16 variant (no model change, routing only) which restores perf while we validate a safe recalibration. We expect to revert within 24h after tests. Apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with a technical summary."

liz: Nice. Can we add expected impact note: perf restored, small cost increase (~+7%)

rahul: Addendum for internal runbook: 
- Immediate: apply per-tenant routing override to fp16-stable (maya/jonas did).
- Short (24h): run a focused recalibration on a sample of customer prompts, enforce fused-kernel eligibility checks, and smoke test latency P95 on canary.
- Medium (48-72h): deploy kernel-selector patch with threshold tweak + telemetry to detect kernel fallback rate. 
- Customer comms: use maya's draft and include cost note.

jonas: I'll open a quick PR to add a metric to show % of matmuls using generic_fp32 vs fused_int8 per endpoint; that'll help track regressions.

ops-bot: deploy 1839004540 started: routing-override/acme -> fp16-stable (canary) :rocket:

maya: ops-bot shows override in progress, customers seeing improvement in telemetry already. Can we block automatic scheduled calibration rollouts for tenant-scoped calibrations until we've validated fix?

rahul: Yes, I'll add a kill-switch to the calibration pipeline to exclude configured tenants. Will also export the failed-layer list for offline analysis.

liz: Good. I'll coordinate CS comms and schedule a short sync with acme for 10am UTC to walk through.

jonas: One more note — we should add a heuristic to batching: if routing variance causes cross-variant splitting, we should coalesce small batches for tenants with high p95 variance. That reduces the overhead while we debug.

maya: Agreed. For now: 1) keep the fp16 override, 2) run focused recalibration, 3) telemetry + selector tweak PR.

liz: Thanks team. I'll post the CS message and update ticket C-8893. :thumbsup:
